# dotsync

> dotsync syncs user-level config between macOS and Linux machines through a cloud folder you already use, such as Nextcloud, OneDrive or Dropbox, by symlinking paths from your home folder into it.

Sync your user-level config between machines through a cloud folder, not git, using symlinks. The complete reference, for people and LLMs, is built into the tool: run `dotsync --llm`.
dotsync is one of the software projects by Jakob Hviid, all listed at https://jakob.hviid.phd/software/ (for LLMs: https://jakob.hviid.phd/llms.txt).

## What it does

- **A mirror of your home folder**: The cloud folder holds a `dotsync/` directory laid out like `$HOME`: `~/.config/zed` lives at `dotsync/.config/zed`. A `dotsync.toml` next to it lists the mappings and syncs with everything else.
- **Each machine picks its own**: A picker lets you tick what to link on this machine, and the symlinks themselves record what is active, so there is no per-machine state file to drift. Mappings can be scoped to one OS, given a different path per OS, and filed in groups.
- **Self-healing links**: When an app saves atomically and replaces a symlink with a real file, `install` and `doctor --fix` relink it if the content still matches the cloud copy. `dotsync undo` reverts the most recent destructive run.
- **Secrets kept out of git**: dotsync never commits anything and refuses a sync folder inside a git repository. Known secrets such as `.ssh`, `.gnupg` and `.aws` get a restrictive mode, re-asserted on `install` and `doctor --fix`.

## Install

Homebrew, on macOS and Linux. Pours a prebuilt binary, so no compiler is needed. The tap is trusted once first, as Homebrew 6 and later ask.

```sh
brew trust --tap jakobhviid/tap
brew install jakobhviid/tap/dotsync
```

Or one line, without Homebrew. No compiler and no root: downloads the prebuilt binary to `~/.local/bin` (set `DOTSYNC_BIN_DIR` to change it).

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jakobhviid/dotsync/main/install.sh | sh
```

Then run it. The first run on each machine finds the cloud folder and opens the picker. Run `dotsync setup` only to re-point the folder or reinstall completions.

```sh
dotsync
```
